validity.recommendation: Downgrade confidence and seek a source that actually names this pipeline; if none surfaces, treat as an unverified/GEM-internal entry. Do not treat the current specs as corroborated.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE NOT INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED. The gem.wiki page carries exactly three references (from wiki_citations.json), none of which name this pipeline: (1) OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 p.75 and (2) OPEC ASB 2010/2011 page79 are country-level oil/gas production/reserves tables and cannot be the origin of a 44 km / 30 in / 220 MMcf/d / 2008 pipeline spec; (3) the steel-network.com Arabic article (now 301-redirecting to steelnetwork.me) is a Jubail industrial-investment news item and, on re-fetch (2026-07-07), does NOT mention Abu Ali, Berri, a 30-in line, 44 km, or 220 MMcf/d — the worklist's earlier ok=true for Capacity/Diameter was a false positive (the verifier matched the bare tokens '220'/'30' on a steel-news page). GulfPub PE World Map (Saudi Arabia's best-covered country, 20 gas features) has NO Abu Ali-Berri entry. All web hits echoing '44 km / 30 in / operating since 2008 / Saudi Aramco' trace back to the gem.wiki page itself (GEM-derived, not independent). The underlying facilities ARE real (Abu Ali Island GOSP/gas-processing; Berri Gas Plant at Jubail), so this is likely a real corridor rather than a pure phantom, but the entity AS DEFINED (these endpoints + these specs) has zero independent support. SECONDARY: potential segment double-count — P7768 'Abu Ali-Berri Gas Pipeline / Sub-sea Pipeline' (added 2025-09-17, 22 km, same 30 in, same 220 MMcf/d) shares the identical name and capacity; P1921 (44 km, 2022 vintage) reads as the whole line and P7768 as its subsea half, so capacity 220 is asserted on both — verify these are a network/segment pair, not a duplication. Also note distinct nearby rows P1922 (Berri-Abu Ali, 8 in) and P1923 (Berri-Abu Ali 2, 10 in) — reverse-named small-diameter lines, probably genuinely separate service, not the same 30-in pipe.

validity.recommendation: Re-examine the end point. Independent Berri-Increment reporting routes Abu Ali associated/sour gas to the Khursaniyah Gas Plant (via the KRT corridor), not to a 'Berri Gas Plant'; the 'Berri' in the name likely refers to the Berri FIELD, not the Berri gas plant. Confirm the true destination facility before trusting End=Berri Gas Plant.
validity.researcher_notes: END-POINT LIKELY MIS-ATTRIBUTED. Independent sources (nsenergybusiness Berri Oil Field Expansion; gcscontracting Khursaniyah Gas Plant & Abu Ali Crude Processing; OGN Berri GOSP expansion) consistently describe Abu Ali Island processing associated/sour gas that is sent to the KHURSANIYAH Gas Plant (stabilized crude to Juaymah terminal), expanding the existing KRT pipeline corridor — none describe an Abu Ali -> 'Berri Gas Plant' gas line. GEM's End=Berri Gas Plant / Al Jubail may conflate the Berri field (which Abu Ali serves) with the Berri gas plant. Owner=Saudi Aramco 100% is safe on general grounds (all Saudi trunk gas infrastructure is Aramco) but no cited source specifically names THIS line as Aramco-owned. FuelSource=Abu Ali Island is consistent with Abu Ali being the origin. Flagging the endpoint delta per standing rule (document, don't overwrite).

routes.corridor_desc: Short (~44 km stated) onshore+offshore link within the Abu Ali / Jubail / Berri industrial cluster of the Eastern Province Gulf coast. Abu Ali is an island connected to the mainland near Jubail; gas leaves the island processing facility and runs into the Jubail-area gas plants. Corridor is only LOOSELY bounded: the origin (Abu Ali Island) is well established, but the destination is uncertain — GEM says Berri Gas Plant (Jubail, ~27.0N 49.6E) while independent Berri-Increment reporting sends Abu Ali associated/sour gas to the Khursaniyah Gas Plant (~27.1N 49.2E) via the KRT pipeline corridor. All coordinates are APPROXIMATE centroids of the named facilities/island (defensible from real places), not surveyed pipeline points. No route geometry sourced; no coordinates fabricated.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named real places: Abu Ali Island (verified as an Aramco gas-processing/GOSP site ~50 km N of Ras Tanura) as origin; destination left as GEM's Berri Gas Plant but flagged because independent sources route Abu Ali gas to Khursaniyah Gas Plant. Coordinates are approximate facility centroids, explicitly not surveyed and not fabricated; a Khursaniyah waypoint is included as the alternative destination. RouteAccuracy should stay low until endpoints are resolved.

summary: P1921 Abu Ali-Berri: existence NOT independently corroborated (cited OPEC ASB + steel-network refs don't name it; GulfPub absent; web hits GEM-derived) + endpoint likely mis-attributed (independent sources send Abu Ali gas to Khursaniyah, not Berri Gas Plant); possible segment double-count with P7768.
